title: Silicon Creations: 15 Years of Learning, Designing and Growing Together - Semiwiki
gist: A first-person culture piece by Silicon Creations' Director of Analog/Mixed-Signal Design Chung-Chun Chen tracing the analog IP vendor's growth from three people in 2011 to nearly 200 employees and almost 600 customers, with forward-looking notes on a 3nm multi-protocol SerDes PMA and expansion into clocking, LC-PLL and sensor IP for AI chips.

insights.claim: Analog/mixed-signal IP vendor Silicon Creations has grown from three people in 2011 (founders Jeff Galloway and Randy Caplan plus one designer) to nearly 200 employees serving almost 600 customers worldwide.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A roughly 600-customer base for a ~200-person private IP firm indicates broad adoption of its clocking/SerDes IP and potential strategic value as an acquisition target.
insights.quote: Today, Silicon Creations has grown to nearly 200 employees across multiple locations and serves almost 600 customers worldwide
insights.locator: When I interviewed with Silicon Creations 15 years ago

insights.claim: Silicon Creations expanded into SerDes around 2011 by hiring an RF-circuit Ph.D. and former Samsung principal engineer, building SerDes architectures largely from scratch.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows how the firm moved from PLL roots into interface IP, now a key product line.
insights.locator: Joining in 2011, I had just left Samsung

insights.claim: Silicon Creations is developing a 3nm SerDes with a multi-protocol PMA to meet increasingly complex customer requirements.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Independent 3nm SerDes IP expands alternatives to large IP vendors for leading-edge interface blocks.

insights.claim: Larger and more complex AI chips are creating demand for connectivity, clocking and monitoring IP, which Silicon Creations is targeting across SerDes, clocking, LC-based PLLs and on-chip voltage and temperature sensors.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI chip complexity lifts demand for supporting analog IP (clocking, sensing), a less crowded niche than compute IP.
insights.quote: As AI chips become larger and more complex, they require technologies for connectivity, clocking, and monitoring.
insights.locator: At the same time, Silicon Creations is expanding beyond the areas

insights.claim: At Silicon Creations, customer field conditions (temperature and supply-voltage ramps, system-level behavior) are fed back into IP designs to make them more robust for subsequent customers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A large installed base compounds into IP robustness, a moat for silicon-proven analog IP vendors.
insights.locator: When you spend most of your time designing circuits

insights.claim: Silicon Creations builds its engineering talent pipeline through university lectures and relationships with professors and students, led by senior designers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Analog design talent is scarce; recruiting pipelines are a competitive factor for small IP firms.
insights.locator: That eventually led to internal lectures and training sessions.

insights.claim: A senior Silicon Creations designer left in 2018 to work with UCLA professor Behzad Razavi at a Silicon Valley company on PAM4 SerDes and full-duplex Ethernet echo cancellation, then returned, showing talent competition for high-speed analog engineers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: High-speed SerDes expertise is contested, and retention/boomerang hires matter for small IP vendors.
insights.locator: Leaving and Choosing to Come Back
